sentences.text:
By means of this bail application the applicant has prayed to be enlarged on bail in Case Crime No.
288 of 2023 at Police Station Ghurpur, District Prayagraj under Sections 376 I.P.C. and Section 3/4 POCSO Act.
The applicant is in jail since 31.08.2023.
The bail application of the applicant was rejected by the learned trial court on 02.02.2024.

The following arguments made by Shri Neeraj Kumar Srivastava, learned counsel and Shri Sunil Prakash Anand, learned counsel on behalf of the applicant, which could not be satisfactorily refuted by Shri Ashok Kumar Yadav, learned counsel on behalf of the victim as part of the free legal aid granted by the High Court Legal Services Committee upon recommendation of the Child Welfare Committee and Shri Paritosh Kumar Malviya, learned AGA-I from the record, entitle the applicant for grant of bail:
1. The victim was wrongly shown as a minor in the prosecution case only to falsely implicate the applicant under the stringent provisions of the POCSO Act and cause his imprisonment.

2. The age of the victim set out in the prosecution case is refuted in light of the judgement of this Court in Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021) and on the following grounds:
(i) There are material contradictions in the age of the victim as recorded in various prosecution documents.
(ii) The age of the victim was incorrectly got registered in the school records by the victim's parents to give her an advantage in life.

entities.text: Monish Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. 55026 of 2021)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There is no legal basis for age related entries in the school records.
The school records disclosing her age as 17 years are unreliable.
(iii) The victim in her statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has asserted that she is 20 years and 17 years of age respectively.
(iv) Medico-legal examination (not the age determination test) records that the victim is 17 years of age.

(v) No medical examination to determine the correct age of the victim as per the latest scientific criteria and medical protocol by eminent doctors from a reputed institution was got done by the prosecution as it would establish the majority of the victim and falsify the prosecution case.
The victim is in fact a major.
3. The victim and the applicant were intimate.

4. The F.I.R. is the result of opposition of the victim's family to the said relationship.

2 5.

entities.text: Azad Kumar Harizan vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The victim in her statements under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. has admitted to intimacy with the applicant.
The victim has also categorically asserted that she has got married to the applicant of her own free will.

6. No allegation of commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has been made in the FIR or in the statements of the victim under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C.
7.
The victim was never confined or bound down in any manner.
The victim was present at various public places but never raised an alarm nor did she resist the applicant.
The conduct of the victim shows that she was a consenting party.
8. Medical evidence to corroborate commission of rape by the applicant with the victim has not been produced by the prosecution.
9. The applicant does not have any criminal history apart from this case.
10. The applicant is not a flight risk.
The applicant being a law abiding citizen has always cooperated with the investigation and undertakes to join the trial proceedings.
There is no possibility of his influencing witnesses, tampering with the evidence or reoffending.
In the light of the preceding discussion and without making any observations on the merits of the case, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant- Azad Kumar Harizan be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number, on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court below.
The following conditions be imposed in the interest of justice:-
( i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence or influence any witness during the trial.
(ii) The applicant will appear before the trial court on the date fixed, unless personal presence is exempted.

The learned trial court is directed to fix the sureties after due application of mind in light of the judgement passed by this Court in Arvind Singh v. State of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Deptt.
(Application U/S 482 No.2613 of 2023).
The learned trial court shall ensure that the right of bail of the applicant granted by this Court is not frustrated by arbitrary demands of sureties, or onerous conditions which are unrelated to the socioeconomic status of the applicant.
Before parting some observations have to be made in the facts of this case.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: This Court is finding that in a large number of undeserving cases, legal aid is being recommended by the Child Welfare Committees even where she is not eligible for the same.
The Child Welfare Committee has to apply its mind before recommending grant of legal aid.
Similarly, this Court is also finding that in many deserving cases legal aid is not being recommended by the Child Welfare Committee.

The Principal Secretary(Law), Government of U.P. as well as the Principal Secretary, Department of Women and Child Development, Government of U.P. shall organize training programs for the Child Welfare Committee members to ensure that they apply their mind to all relevant considerations before recommending legal aid.
